linkedin.post:
Most frontend performance problems trace back to one habit: doing work on every event.

A search box that calls your API on every keystroke will hammer the backend and rate-limit real users. Debounce fixes it by waiting for a pause, then running once.

→ Wrap the handler in a debounce (a closure over a timer)
→ Every keystroke clears the pending timer and starts a new one
→ The callback runs only after the user goes quiet (e.g. 300ms)
→ Reach for it on search-as-you-type, resize/scroll handlers, and auto-save

Rule of thumb: debounce waits for quiet, throttle runs at a fixed interval. Pick by the behavior you want.
